approach: Get the string-length constraint linking m1's motion up the incline to m2's fall, then combine it with Newton's second law for m1, the movable pulley, and m2.

steps.text: The cord from m1 goes over the fixed corner pulley down to the movable pulley; the second cord passes over the top of the hanging pulley; one segment runs down to the fixed bracket and the other runs down to m2.
steps.equation: cord 1: m1 to fixed pulley to movable pulley; cord 2: fixed bracket to movable pulley to m2

steps.text: If m1 moves a distance x up the incline, the movable pulley must move down by x (cord 1 is fixed length), and then both segments of cord 2 shorten or lengthen by that same x, so m2 must move down by 2x.
steps.why_this_step: This is the constraint relation: it links every acceleration in the system before any force equation is written.

steps.text: The hanging pulley is massless, so the single upward pull T₁ from cord 1 at its axle must balance the two downward pulls T₂ from the segments of cord 2.
Write Newton's second law for m1 along the frictionless incline, taking up the slope as positive.
steps.equation: T1 − m1 g sinθ = m1 a1

steps.text: Write Newton's second law for m2, taking downward as positive.
Substitute T1 = 2T2 and m2 = ηm1 into both equations and eliminate T2 to solve for a1.
steps.equation: T2 = ηm1(g − 2a1); T1 = m1(a1 + g sinθ) = 2T2 gives a1(1 + 4η) = g(2η − sinθ)

steps.text: So a1 = g(2η − sinθ)/(1 + 4η), and m2's acceleration is twice that.
steps.equation: a2 = 2g(2η − sinθ)/(1 + 4η), directed downward when 2η > sinθ; upward when 2η < sinθ

final_answer.value: a2 = 2g(2η − sinθ)/(1 + 4η), directed downward when 2η > sinθ; when 2η < sinθ the expression is negative and m₂ accelerates upward (the acceleration of the mass m2 = ηm1)

common_mistakes.text: Missing the movable-pulley factor of 2 in the constraint and taking a2 = a1, which gives a1(1 + 2η) = g(2η − sinθ), the wrong denominator (1 + 2η) instead of (1 + 4η).
